title: Spreading a prelog homomorphism and a stalk chart without Noetherian hypotheses
statement: Let $X$ be any scheme, $\bar x$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and $M$ an fs log structure with the arbitrary-scheme chart meaning of [lem-per-associated-log-arbitrary-scheme]. Write $L=M_{\bar x}$ and $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$. Let $B$ be a finitely generated commutative monoid. Every homomorphism $B\to L$ is the germ of a homomorphism $B\to\Gamma(U,M)$ on a pointed etale neighbourhood $(U,\bar u)$ of $\bar x$. Two homomorphisms from $B$ on such a neighbourhood with equal germs agree after a further pointed etale restriction. Any finite collection of these choices and equalities can be realized on one common neighbourhood. If $B$ is integral and a specified homomorphism $c:B\to L$ induces an isomorphism $B\oplus_{(\alpha c)^{-1}(A^\times)}A^\times\xrightarrow{\sim}L$, then $c$ lifts, after pointed etale restriction, to a chart $B\to M|_U$. If $B$ is fine saturated, this is an fs chart. A pointed etale neighbourhood means an etale scheme $U\to X$ together with a geometric point above $\bar x$ [def-weil-etale-morphism]. No local Noetherian assumption on $X$ or $U$ is made.

source.place: ILO VI 1.1, printed p.69, and VIII 3.3.4, printed p.107 (etale-local charts); Kato (1988), section 2, stalk chart criterion. Agent refinement isolating finite-presentation spreading without a Noetherian hypothesis.

proof.text: Work first with any sheaf $F$ of commutative monoids on $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$, not necessarily a log structure. Use the small-site universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]; pointed objects form a small category as well, since lifts from the fixed geometric point into each object form a set. The stalk is the underlying-set colimit of sections [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], and its index category is filtered [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered]. Thus every stalk element has a section representative, and equality of two germs becomes equality after a pointed refinement [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise]. Repeated common refinements realize any finite list of representatives and equalities together, also refining an initially specified neighbourhood. For two sections on the same object use clause (3) of the elementwise lemma, so both restrict along the same arrow. These assertions apply to several sheaves simultaneously. On an etale neighbourhood $j:U\to X$, restriction is inverse image on underlying sets [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-restriction], and [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-stalk-germ] identifies its pointed stalk with the original stalk, compatibly with represented germs. The identifications respect monoid products and identities because these are represented by products and identities of sections.

source.place: Tag 03PQ, lemma-cofinal-etale; definition-stalk and its following paragraph; Tag 03S2, section-extension-by-zero, restriction convention. Elementwise colimits: categories.tex, Tag 04AX, section-directed-colimits.

proof.text: Choose generators $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ of $B$. By [lem-trf-fg-commutative-monoid-finite-presentation] there are finitely many pairs $(a_j,d_j)\in\mathbf N^r\times\mathbf N^r$ presenting all relations among these generators. Given $c:B\to F_{\bar x}$, Step 1 represents the finitely many $c(b_i)$ by sections $s_i$ on one pointed neighbourhood. For each relation the two sections $\prod_i s_i^{(a_j)_i}$ and $\prod_i s_i^{(d_j)_i}$ have equal germs, since $c$ is a homomorphism. Step 1 makes all these finitely many equalities hold on one further neighbourhood. The universal-property clause of the finite-presentation lemma now gives a homomorphism $\widetilde c:B\to F(U)$ with $\widetilde c(b_i)=s_i$. Its germ is $c$, since these homomorphisms agree on the generators. The presentation result is for arbitrary finitely generated commutative monoids, so no integrality of $B$ or $F(U)$ was used. In particular this proves the first assertion with $F=M$.

source.place: definition-stalk and paragraph after it, together with the existing finite-monoid-presentation input; agent finite-generators/finite-relations argument.

proof.text: If two homomorphisms $B\to F(U)$ have the same germ, their values on each of the finitely many $b_i$ have equal germs. Step 1 makes these finitely many pairs equal after one pointed restriction; agreement on generators gives agreement on all of $B$. Given finitely many lifting problems and equalities, perform the construction of Step 2 for each, take a common pointed refinement as in Step 1, then impose all the finitely many requested generator equalities on one further refinement. Restrictions preserve the relations already imposed. This proves the equality and simultaneous-choice assertions, still for any $F$. Empty lists and the trivial monoid require no equations and can be realized on the initial neighbourhood.

source.place: Agent elementary finite iteration of Steps 1--2.

proof.text: Now assume $B$ integral and the stipulated stalk pushout map is an isomorphism. Lift the specified $c$ by Step 2. Put $\beta=\alpha\widetilde c$ and $N=L_U(B,\beta)$. By [lem-per-integral-chart-logification-thickening], $N$ is a fine integral log structure and its universal property gives $f:N\to M|_U$ over the identity of $U$, with $f\iota_B=\widetilde c$. Its stalk formula identifies $f_{\bar u}$ with the assumed map $B\oplus_{(\alpha c)^{-1}(A^\times)}A^\times\to L$; hence $f_{\bar u}$ is an isomorphism. By the fs chart meaning in [lem-per-associated-log-arbitrary-scheme], $M|_U$ has an etale covering with charts $q:Q\to M(V)$ by fine saturated monoids $Q$. The geometric-point lifting assertion [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift] supplies a pointed member of that covering. Replace $U$ by this member. Restriction of $N$ is the associated log structure of the restricted $\beta$, by the restriction clause of the logification lemma; all specified germs are retained by Step 1. We now have both the fixed $B$-presentation of $N$ and a fine chart $q$ of $M|_U$.

source.place: VI 1.1, printed p.69 (chart meaning), VIII Remark 3.3.4(ii), printed p.107 (etale-local charts), and VI 3.7(a), printed p.75, final chart-extension sentence. Agent associated-log construction of the comparison.

proof.text: The inverse stalk homomorphism gives $k_0=f_{\bar u}^{-1}q_{\bar u}:Q\to N_{\bar u}$. Apply the already proved Step 2 to the sheaf of monoids $N$ on $U$ and the finitely generated monoid $Q$, obtaining $k:Q\to N(V)$ with germ $k_0$. The two homomorphisms $fk,q:Q\to M(V)$ have the same germ, so Step 3 makes $fk=q$ on a further pointed refinement. Since $f$ respects structure maps, $\alpha_Nk=\alpha_Mq$ there. The universal property of [lem-per-integral-chart-logification-thickening], applied to the integral chart monoid $Q$, therefore extends $k$ uniquely to a log homomorphism $g:M|_V\to N|_V$ over the identity, with $gq=k$. The two log homomorphisms $fg$ and the identity of $M|_V$ agree on $q$, since $fgq=fk=q$; the same uniqueness clause gives $fg=\mathrm{id}$. On the pointed stalk, $f_{\bar v}$ is invertible and $f_{\bar v}g_{\bar v}=\mathrm{id}$, so $g_{\bar v}=f_{\bar v}^{-1}$.

source.place: VI 3.7(a), printed p.75, final chart-extension sentence; agent inverse-map construction via the associated-log universal property.

proof.text: The two maps $gf\iota_B,\iota_B:B\to N(V)$ have equal germs because $g_{\bar v}f_{\bar v}=\mathrm{id}$. Step 3, now for the sheaf $N$ and the finitely generated monoid $B$, makes these maps equal on one further pointed refinement $W$. The universal property of [lem-per-integral-chart-logification-thickening] for the $B$-presentation of $N|_W$ then gives $gf=\mathrm{id}_{N|_W}$. Thus $f$ and $g$ are inverse log homomorphisms on $W$. By the chart meaning of [lem-per-associated-log-arbitrary-scheme], the restricted lift $\widetilde c:B\to M(W)$ is a chart, and its germ is the specified $c$. If $B$ is fine saturated, a chart by this very monoid is an fs chart by that definition. The argument used finite presentations of $B$ and $Q$, not of a unit group or of $N(V)$; every cited geometric and logification statement applies to arbitrary schemes, so no local Noetherian hypothesis has entered.
